gen-mystery-quest-gf-mada: Mada reads with curves that refuse to close and a midzone that towers over everything around it. Mystery Quest sits above in its bookish, nostalgic display voice, and a long page would feel like a storybook set in plain sans.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-martel-sans: Open jaws on every curved stroke give Mystery Quest a nostalgic, bookish look, with compact ascenders tucked above tall lowercase. Martel Sans follows with generous openings in each curve, so a long page would move along in a modern, unfussy plain sans.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-matangi: Mystery Quest has open jaws on every curve and a low y tail. Matangi underneath is a sans-serif with twine-like strokes and a hefty lowercase, whose y tail matches its arm in thickness, so the two feel like old storybook and fresh signage.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-maven-pro: Storybook curves meet a modern line: Mystery Quest keeps its open jaws and compact ascenders, while Maven Pro draws its curves and straights at one width. Its welcoming c keeps a long read light.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-michroma: Mystery Quest leaves open jaws on every curved stroke, which gives its nostalgic, bookish heading a hand-lettered feel. Michroma's wide berth between letters makes a long page feel spacious in a sans.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre has the weight of drawn wire, with horizontals and verticals matching and a lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals. Mystery Quest, with its low contrast, adds a bookish, nostalgic note on top.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Wire-smooth and bright, Mochiy Pop One has a very large lowercase eye and a single stroke width throughout. Mystery Quest, though, is the one that does bookish, nostalgic drama best, while this sans-serif simply carries the sentences.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Mochiy Pop P One reads wide and sizable, with space between letters. Mystery Quest brings bookish, nostalgic open jaws to meet that monoline sans-serif, and they feel like a storybook beside a friendly sign.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-montserrat-underlin: Professional in tone, Montserrat Underline has breathing counters and round bowls of constant width, with a lowercase that looks oversized beside its capitals. Its strongest quality is that marker-like line, which Mystery Quest softens.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-mozilla-headline: Approachable is the first word for Mozilla Headline, with its big-bodied lowercase and splayed c terminal, under Mystery Quest's bookish open jaws. Mozilla Headline's strongest quality is that friendly, oversized lowercase, which sets it apart from the nostalgic heading.
